rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guards find the youths prostrating in their prayer place, weeping and asking God to save them from Daqyanus and his faction.
rows.anchor: وكانوا قد دخلوا في مصلى لهم فوجدوهم سجودا على وجوههم يبكون ويتضرعون إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daqyanus demands that the youths sacrifice to the idols or face execution.
rows.anchor: اختاروا إما أن تذبحوا لآلهتنا كما ذبح الناس وإما أن أقتلكم

rows.speaker: مكسلمينا
rows.claim: Their eldest, Maksalmina, declares that they worship only the Lord of heaven and earth and will never accept the tyrant's idols.
rows.anchor: فقال مكسلمينا- وكان أكبرهم-: إن لنا إلها ملأ السماوات والأرض عظمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companions of Maksalmina answer Daqyanus with the same confession of faith.
rows.anchor: ثم قال أصحاب مكسلمينا لدقيانوس مثل ما قال له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruler postpones punishment because they are young, strips their rank clothing and gold and silver adornments, and gives them time to reconsider.
rows.anchor: ثم أمر بحلية كانت عليهم من ذهب وفضة فنزعت منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fearing Daqyanus's return, the youths decide to take household provisions, give some away, and retreat to a nearby cave to worship God.
rows.anchor: فائتمروا بينهم أن يأخذ كل رجل نفقة من بيت أبيه فيتصدقوا بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths take their remaining provisions to the cave, and their dog follows them.
rows.anchor: وانطلقوا بما بقي معهم من نفقتهم، وأتبعهم كلب كان لهم

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Ka'b relates that a dog repeatedly follows them, says it loves God's beloved, and offers to guard them while they sleep.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار: مروا بكلب فنبح عليهم فطردوه، فعاد ففعلوا ذلك مرارا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says seven youths flee Daqyanus by night when he summons them to worship idols; a believing shepherd and his dog join them.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هربوا ليلا من دقيانوس بن جلانوس حيث دعاهم إلى عبادة الأصنام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The youths live in the cave praying and praising God, while Tamlikha secretly buys food and checks whether the ruler has mentioned them.
rows.anchor: فلبثوا فيه ليس لهم عمل إلا الصلاة والتسبيح والتكبير والتحميد ابتغاء وجه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Tamlikha disguises himself in poor clothing when entering the city to buy their food and hear the news.
rows.anchor: ثم يأخذ ورقة فينطلق إلى المدينة فيشتري طعاما وشرابا ويسمع ويتجسس لهم الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Daqyanus returns and threatens the believers, Tamlikha reports the danger; the youths prostrate and seek God's protection from trial.
rows.anchor: فزعوا ووقعوا سجودا يدعون الله عز وجل ويتضرعون ويتعوذون به من الفتنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At sunset God causes the youths and their dog to sleep in the cave, with their provisions beside their heads.
rows.anchor: فبينا هم على ذلك إذ ضرب الله على آذانهم في الكهف وكلبهم باسط ذراعيه بباب الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daqyanus cannot find the youths the next day, and the city's leaders accuse them of stubborn rebellion despite his offered reprieve.
rows.anchor: فقال له عظماء المدينة: ما أنت بحقيق أن ترحم قوما فجرة مردة عصاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths' parents say their sons spent the money in the city and withdrew to Mount Yanjalus; the ruler releases the parents.
rows.anchor: ذهبوا بأموالنا وأهلكوها في أسواق المدينة ثم انطلقوا فارتقوا إلى جبل يدعى ينجلوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspires Daqyanus to seal the cave, intending to honor the youths as a sign to a later community and proof that resurrection will come.
rows.anchor: أراد الله عز وجل أن يكرمهم ويجعلهم آية لأمة يستخلف من بعدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daqyanus orders the entrance sealed so the youths die of thirst and hunger, believing them awake; God has taken their souls in a sleep-like death.
rows.anchor: قد توفى الله أرواحهم وفاة النوم وكلبهم باسط ذراعيه بالوصيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two secret believers in the royal household, Biedros and Rutas, record the youths' names, lineage, and story on lead and hide it in a copper chest for future believers.
rows.anchor: اسم أحدهما بيدروس، واسم الآخر روتاس ائتمرا أن يكتبا شأن الفتية وأنسابهم وأسماءهم

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr describes noble, adorned youths who secretly came to faith during a festival where their people displayed idols.
rows.anchor: وقال عبيد بن عمير: كان أصحاب الكهف فتيانا مطوقين مسورين ذوي ذوائب

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: In Ubayd ibn Umayr's account, the youths separately confide their faith to one another and discover that they share one belief.
rows.anchor: ثم قالوا: ليخرج كل فتيين منكم فيخلوا ثم ليفش كل واحد منكم إلى صاحبه

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: The youths find a nearby cave and enter with a hunting dog, saying God will spread mercy and provide a suitable way forward; they sleep 309 years.
rows.anchor: فأووا إلى الكهف ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته ويهيئ لكم من أمركم مرفقا

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Their people lose the youths' tracks and preserve a record of their names and disappearance in the king's treasury.
rows.anchor: فلما لم يقدموا كتب أحدهم في لوح: فلان وفلان أبناء ملوكنا

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb says a disciple of Jesus avoids a city's idol, works at a bathhouse, and teaches young men about heaven, earth, and the afterlife until they believe.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه: جاء أحد حواري عيسى بن مريم (عليه السلام) الى مدينة أصحاب الكهف

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: In Wahb's account, the disciple rebukes the prince's son for entering a bath with a woman; both die there, and the disciple is blamed and pursued.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه: جاء أحد حواري عيسى بن مريم

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: The pursued young believers escape with a fellow believer working in a field and his dog, reach a cave at night, and sleep there by God's act.
rows.anchor: فمروا بصاحب لهم في زرع وهو على مثل إيمانهم فذكروا له أنهم التمسوا

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb says the king's men are terrified whenever they try to enter the cave, so they seal the entrance and leave the youths to die.
rows.anchor: وكلما أراد الرجل منهم دخوله أرعب، فلم يطق أحد دخوله

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: A shepherd later opens the cave to shelter his flock from rain; God restores the youths' souls the next morning.
rows.anchor: ثم إن راعيا أدركه المطر عند الكهف فقال: لو فتحت هذا الكهف فأدخلته غنمي من المطر

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Theodosius ruled 38 years as people split over bodily resurrection; as deniers gained influence, he prayed in sackcloth and ashes for a clarifying sign.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: ثم ملك أهل تلك البلاد رجل صالح يقال له تيدوسيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God intends to reveal the cave youths to vindicate Theodosius's faith and make their revival a sign that the Hour and resurrection are real.
rows.anchor: أراد أن يظهر على الفتية أصحاب الكهف ويبين للناس شأنهم ويجعلهم آية له وحجة عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man named Olyas is prompted to remove the structure covering the cave so he can build a sheep pen from its stones.
rows.anchor: وكان اسم ذلك الرجل أولياس- أن يهدم ذلك البنيان الذي على فم الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the cave opens, God screens the sleepers from people with terror; even the bravest cannot pass the sleeping dog at the entrance.
rows.anchor: فحجبهم الله تعالى من الناس بالرعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths wake joyful, pray as before, and still think Daqyanus is pursuing them; they ask Tamlikha what happened the prior evening.
rows.anchor: فجلسوا فرحين مسفرة وجوههم طيبة أنفسهم، فسلم بعضهم على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They suppose they slept a day or part of one, while Tamlikha says the city searched for them and the tyrant plans to sacrifice or kill them.
rows.anchor: وتلطف ولا تشعرن بنا أحدا، وابتع لنا طعاما فائتنا به

rows.speaker: مكسلمينا
rows.claim: Maksalmina warns his companions that they will meet God and must not renounce their faith if summoned the next day.
rows.anchor: رأى حجارة منزوعة عن باب الكهف فعجب منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They send Tamlikha to learn the news and buy more food discreetly, since their earlier supply was too small.
rows.anchor: انطلق إلى المدينة فتسمع ما يقال [عنا] بها اليوم وما الذي نذكر به عند دقيانوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamlikha carries old coins bearing Daqyanus's stamp and notices stones removed from the cave entrance, but does not know the tyrant died 300 years earlier.
rows.anchor: وكانت كخفاف الربع. فانطلق تمليخا خارجا فلما مر بباب الكهف رأى حجارة منزوعة عن باب الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamlikha sees Christian signs over the gates and hears people openly invoke Jesus, unlike the persecution he remembers from the previous evening.
rows.anchor: فرأى فوق ظهر الباب علامة تكون لأهل الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He concludes the city may not be the one he knew; its name is Daphsus, and he fears he has lost his reason.
rows.anchor: اسم هذه المدينة يا فتى؟ قال: دفسوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Merchants pass his ancient coins from hand to hand and suspect he has found an old treasure, then threaten to take him before the authorities.
rows.anchor: ثم جعلوا يتطارحونها من رجل إلى رجل، ويعجبون منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crowd binds Tamlikha and says he is unknown in the city; he waits for his family, certain they lived there the previous evening.
rows.anchor: فجعلوا ينظرون إليه ويقولون: والله ما هذه الفتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crowd takes him to the two city leaders, the righteous Armos and Astius; he mistakes them for Daqyanus and prays for patience and support.
rows.anchor: وهما رجلان صالحان اسم أحدهما أرموس واسم الآخر أسطيوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamlikha grieves that he is separated from companions with whom he had pledged never to renounce God, worship idols, or part in life or death.
rows.anchor: وقد كنا تواثقنا على ألا نفترق في حياة ولا موت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city leaders think Tamlikha's coin is from a treasure because its stamp is more than 300 years old, and threaten torture unless he confesses.
rows.anchor: هذا الورق ونقشها أكثر من ثلاثمائة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamlikha explains that Daqyanus forced them toward idol worship and asks the leaders to accompany him to the cave; Armos recognizes a possible divine sign.
rows.anchor: يا قوم لعل هذه آية من آيات الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths hear the approaching crowd and fear Daqyanus has come for them; they pray, then meet the returning Tamlikha with Armos and the townspeople.
rows.anchor: فبينا هم يظنون ذلك ويتخوفون إذ سمعوا الأصوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After hearing Tamlikha, the youths realize God had kept them asleep for the whole period so their awakening could affirm resurrection and the coming Hour.
rows.anchor: فعرفوا عند ذلك أنهم كانوا نياما بأمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Armos opens the sealed lead record, which identifies the seven youths and explains that Daqyanus sealed them in the cave for refusing to abandon faith.
rows.anchor: فوجدوا فيه لوحين من رصاص مكتوبا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The townspeople praise God for showing them a sign of resurrection and find the youths seated, radiant, and with clothing unspoiled.
rows.anchor: مشرقة وجوههم، لم تبل ثيابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Armos and the townspeople urgently summon Theodosius to witness the youths as a sign of resurrection; the king rises relieved and thanks God for preserving the faith inherited from his forebears.
rows.anchor: ثم إن أرموس وأصحابه بعثوا بريدا إلى ملكهم الصالح تيدوسيس أن عجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king and the townspeople travel to the cave, where the youths rejoice, prostrate, greet him, and commend his rule to God's protection.
rows.anchor: فلما رأى الفتية تيدوسيس فرحوا به وخروا سجدا على وجوههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths bid the king farewell and ask God to preserve him and protect him from the harm of jinn and people.
rows.anchor: نستودعك الله، ونقرأ عليك السلام، وحفظك الله وحفظ ملكك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the king stands, God takes the youths' lives again; after they reject golden coffins in a dream, he orders a teak coffin and they remain hidden by terror.
rows.anchor: إنا لم نخلق من ذهب ولا فضة، ولكنا خلقنا من تراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king orders a mosque built at the cave entrance and establishes a major annual feast for the youths.
rows.anchor: وأمر الملك فجعل على باب الكهف مسجد يصلى فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant says Tamlikha enters alone to reassure the youths; God takes their lives, conceals their location, and no one can find them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنهم لما أتوا إلى باب الكهف قال تمليخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Muhammad asks God to let him see the sleepers; God instead directs him to send four eminent companions to convey his message and invite them to believe.
rows.anchor: ويقال: إن نبي الله محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم سأل ربه أن يريه إياهم

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: Gabriel instructs Muhammad to seat Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, and Abu Dharr on the corners of a cloth and summon Solomon's gentle wind.
rows.anchor: ابسط كساء لهم، وأجلس على طرف من أطرافها أبا بكر، وعلى الثاني عمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind carries the four companions to the cave; the dog welcomes them, and God restores the youths' souls when they greet them.
rows.anchor: فحملتهم الريح حتى انطلقت بهم إلى باب الكهف

rows.speaker: أصحاب الكهف
rows.claim: The youths return the greeting, accept Muhammad's message and Islam, and send him their greetings before resuming their sleep until the end time.
rows.anchor: فآمنوا بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، وقبلوا دين الإسلام، وقالوا: أقرئوا محمدا منا السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant says the Mahdi will greet the youths, God will revive them, and they will sleep again until resurrection.
rows.anchor: ويقال: إن المهدي يسلم عليهم، فيحييهم الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: أصحاب النبي
rows.claim: When Muhammad asks what happened, the companions report that the youths answered his greeting, accepted his prophethood, and praised God for sending him.
rows.anchor: فأجابوا وأنابوا وشهدوا أنك رسول الله حقا

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet prays not to be separated from his in-laws, loved ones, family, and companions, and asks forgiveness for those who love him and his household.
rows.anchor: اللهم لا تفرق بيني وبين أصهاري وأحبائي وأختاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths' taking refuge means going and joining the cave, a cavern in Mount Yanjalus called Khayram.
rows.anchor: إذ أوى أي صار وانضم الفتية إلى الكهف، وهو غار في جبل ينجلوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prayer asks God to ease for them what they seek of His good pleasure.
rows.anchor: أي يسر لنا ما نلتمس من رضاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets right guidance as a safe way out of the cave.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: رشدا أي مخرجا من الغار في سلامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes rushd to mean correctness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: صوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is a rhetorically unmatched Qur'anic expression meaning that God made the youths sleep and imposed sleep on them.
rows.anchor: هذا من فصيحات القرآن التي أقرت العرب بالقصور عن الإتيان بمثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation says God blocked hearing and stopped sound from reaching them, describing sleepers or the dead.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه حجبناهم عن السمع، وسددنا نفوذ الصوت إلى مسامعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom can mean that God sent an affliction upon someone, as in saying He struck him with paralysis.
rows.anchor: كما يقال: ضرب الله فلان بالفالج، أي ابتلاه به وأرسله عليه

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub compares the phrase to an Arab idiom for a ruler restraining subjects or a master stopping a servant's authorized trade.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب: هو كقول العرب: ضرب الأمير علي يد الرعية

rows.speaker: الأسود بن يعفر
rows.claim: Al-Aswad ibn Ya'far's line uses 'struck the earth upon me with barriers' as poetic evidence for the idiom.
rows.anchor: قال الأسود بن يعفر، وكان ضريرا: ومن الحوادث لا أبا لك أنني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adadan means counted years and is an adjective; the author distinguishes the verbal noun from the noun for what is counted.
rows.anchor: سنين عددا أي معدودة، وهو نعت للسنين، فالعد المصدر، والعدد الاسم المعدود

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda parses adadan as an accusative verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: هو نصب على المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God awakens them so the two groups can be tested over which better reckoned the time they remained asleep in the cave.
rows.anchor: ثم بعثناهم، يعني من نومهم لنعلم أي الحزبين أحصى لما لبثوا أمدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier Muslim group says the youths stayed 309 years, while a later group disputes the duration; the earlier group finally says God knows best.
rows.anchor: فقال المسلمون الأولون: مكثوا في كهفهم ثلاثمائة سنة وتسع سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two parties are the two groups; ahsa means more accurate or better at remembering, and amad means an endpoint.
rows.anchor: أصوب وأحفظ لما لبثوا في كهفهم نياما، أمدا: غاية

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses amad as a number or count.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: عددا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative on amad can be parsed either as specification or as governed by the preceding phrase about how long they stayed.
rows.anchor: وفي نصبه وجهان: أحدهما على التفسير والثاني لوقوع لما لبثوا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an recounts and reveals the true report about the cave companions.
rows.anchor: نحن نقص، أي نقرأ وننزل عليك نبأهم، أي خبر أصحاب الكهف بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are called youths because they were young men who believed; the author says God granted them that description upon believing without intermediary.
rows.anchor: حكم الله لهم بالفتوة حين آمنوا بلا واسطة لذلك

rows.speaker: أهل اللسان
rows.claim: The language scholars say faith is the foundation of futuwwa.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل اللسان: رأس الفتوة الإيمان

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Al-Junayd defines futuwwa as refraining from harm, giving generously, and not complaining.
rows.anchor: وقال الجنيد: الفتوة كف الأذى وبذل الندى، وترك الشكوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One definition says futuwwa consists of avoiding forbidden acts and practicing noble deeds.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الفتوة شيئان: اجتناب المحارم، واستعمال المكارم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another definition says a youth neither claims virtue before acting nor praises himself after acting.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الفتى من لا يدعي قبل الفعل، ولا يزكي نفسه بعد الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A saying distinguishes spiritual courage from merely enduring lashes: the true youth is one who crosses the bridge.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ليس الفتى من يصبر على السياط، إنما الفتى من جاز على الصراط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another saying defines true youth by feeding the poor rather than merely enduring the knife.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ليس الفتى من يصبر على السكين، إنما الفتى من يطعم المسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God increases the youths in guidance by increasing their faith, insight, and certainty.
rows.anchor: وزدناهم هدى إيمانا وبصيرة وإيقانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God strengthens their hearts with patience and the light of faith so they can leave comfortable homes and their people for the cave.
rows.anchor: وشددنا على قلوبهم بالصبر، وألهمناهم ذلك، وقويناهم بنور الإيمان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil gloss shatat as injustice or wrong.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: جورا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses shatat as a lie.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: كذبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of shatat means going beyond the proper measure and excess.
rows.anchor: وأصل الشطط والإشطاط: مجاوزة القدر، والإفراط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths say their people worship idols besides God and should produce clear proof for doing so; the worst fabricator claims God has partners or a child.
rows.anchor: لولا يأتون عليهم أي هلا يأتون على عبادتهم بسلطان بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths urge one another to leave their people and the idols they worship besides God, then take refuge in the cave.
rows.anchor: يعني قومكم وما يعبدون إلا الله، أي واعتزلتم أصنامهم التي يعبدونها من دون الله

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: The codex of Abdullah ibn Masud adds 'besides God' after the phrase about what the people worship.
rows.anchor: وكذلك هو في مصحف عبد الله: (وما يعبدون من دون الله)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are told to go to the cave; God will extend mercy and arrange a comfortable provision or resource for them.
rows.anchor: ينشر، أي يبسط لكم ويظهر لكم ربكم من رحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word marfiqan means something a person uses for comfort or support, and has two vocalized forms.
rows.anchor: والمرفق: ما يرتفق به الإنسان، وفيه لغتان: مرفق، ومرفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun's course and cave conditions are among God's wonders and proofs of His power and wisdom.
rows.anchor: من عجائب صنع الله ودلالات قدرته وحكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance and misguidance belong to God; whoever God guides is guided, and the misled person has no directing guardian.
rows.anchor: لأن التوفيق والخذلان بيد الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths appear awake though sleeping; yaqaz and ruqud are plural forms for alert and sleeping people, respectively.
rows.anchor: وتحسبهم يا محمد أيقاظا أي منتبهين، جمع يقظ ويقظ

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads the verb for turning them with a lightened consonant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن (ونقلبهم) بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they were turned onto a different side once each year to keep the ground from consuming their flesh.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كانوا ينقلبون في السنة مرة إلى جانب من جانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says their turning took place on Ashura.
rows.anchor: ويقال: إن يوم عاشوراء كان يوم تقليبهم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says they were turned twice each year.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة: كان لهم في كل سنة تقليبان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes the dog as brindled.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان أنمر

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the dog was yellow.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كان أصفر

rows.speaker: القرظي
rows.claim: Al-Qurazi says its strong yellow color tended toward red.
rows.anchor: وقال القرظي: شدة صفرته تضرب إلى الحمرة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi compares the dog's color to khilinj wood.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: لونه كالخلنج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports compare the dog's color to stone or to the sky.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لون الحجر. وقيل: لون السماء

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali says the dog's name was Rayyan.
rows.anchor: وقال علي ابن أبي طالب (رضي الله عنه) : «كان اسمه ريان»

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas gives the dog the name Qitmir.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: قطمير

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي
rows.claim: Al-Awza'i gives the dog's name as Natwa.
rows.anchor: وقال الأوزاعي: نتوى

rows.speaker: شعيب الجبائي
rows.claim: Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i gives the dog's name as Hamran.
rows.anchor: وقال شعيب الجبائي: حمران

rows.speaker: عبد الله ابن كثير
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Kathir gives the dog's name as Qatmur.
rows.anchor: عبد الله ابن كثير: اسم الكلب قطمور

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi gives the dog's name as Nun.
rows.anchor: [قال] السدي: نون. عبد الله بن سلام: بسيط

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Salam gives the dog's name as Basit.
rows.anchor: عبد الله بن سلام: بسيط

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka'b gives the dog's name as Ashhab.
rows.anchor: كعب: أصهب

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb gives the dog's name as Naqiya, while another report calls it Qutayfir.
rows.anchor: وهب: نقيا، وقيل: قطفير

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar reports protective invocations associated with a scorpion and a dog, including reciting the cave dog's description when a dog attacks.
rows.anchor: عن عمر قال: إن مما أخذ على العقرب ألا يضر بأحد في ليله ونهاره

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Ja'far al-Sadiq reads kalibahum, meaning the dog's owner or keeper.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جعفر الصادق (وكالبهم) يعني: صاحب الكلب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Dahhak say al-wasid is the forecourt of the cave; this is also transmitted from Ibn Abbas through Ali ibn Abi Talha.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد والضحاك: الوصيد: فناء الكهف

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr interprets al-wasid as the ground or soil, a view transmitted from Ibn Abbas through Atiyya al-Awfi.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: الوصيد الصعيد، وهو التراب

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says al-wasid means the door, transmitted from Ibn Abbas through Ikrima.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: الوصيد الباب، وهي رواية عكرمة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says al-wasid is the threshold of the doorway.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: الوصيد: عتبة الباب

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybi says al-wasid is the building and relates it to the Arabic verbs for closing a door.
rows.anchor: وقال القتيبي الوصيد: البناء، وأصله من قول العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about turning away means God made the sleepers' appearance prevent anyone from reaching or touching them until the appointed time, when they would become a sign.
rows.anchor: حتى لا يصل إليهم واصل، ولا تلمسهم يد لامس حتى يبلغ الكتاب أجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rعب means fear; Medina readers use a doubled form for 'you would be filled,' and explanations include the place's eerie look, open eyes, or God's protective terror.
rows.anchor: ولملئت منهم رعبا: خوفا، وقرأ أهل المدينة: (لملئت) بالتشديد

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the youths' open eyes make them look like sleepers about to speak, causing terror.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: لأن أعينهم مفتحة- كالمستيقظ الذي يريد أن يتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says God protected the youths from being seen by frightening people away.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الله تعالى منعهم بالرعب لئلا يراهم أحد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas tells that on a Roman campaign Muawiya wanted to uncover the cave, but Ibn Abbas said God had barred someone better than Muawiya from seeing them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ليس ذلك لك، قد منع الله من هو خير منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Muawiya sent men to inspect the cave, a wind drove them out and terror prevented them from seeing the youths.
rows.anchor: فبعث ناسا فقال: اذهبوا فانظروا. ففعلوا، فلما دخلوا الكهف بعث الله عز وجل عليهم ريحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God preserved their bodies and clothes from decay through the long sleep, He awakens them so they can talk and question one another.
rows.anchor: وحفظنا أجسامهم من البلى على طول الزمان، وثيابهم من العفن على مر الأيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maksalmina, their leader, asks how long they slept because the duration seems strange; another explanation is that they missed a prayer.
rows.anchor: قال قائل منهم يعني: رئيسهم مكسلمينا: كم لبثتم في نومكم؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say a day or part of one because they entered in the morning, saw some sun remaining, and wished not to claim more than they knew.
rows.anchor: لأنهم دخلوا الكهف غدوة، فلما رأوا الشمس قالوا: أو بعض يوم توقيا من الكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing that their hair and nails had grown, they realize the sleep lasted longer and say their Lord knows best; another account has their leader end the disagreement this way.
rows.anchor: فلما نظروا إلى شعورهم وأظفارهم تيقنوا أن لبثهم أكثر من يوم أو بعض يوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waraq means silver, whether struck into coins or unminted; the author cites the Prophetic instruction that a companion replace a festering silver nose with gold.
rows.anchor: والورق: الفضة مضروبة كانت أو غير مضروبة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة وخلف
rows.claim: Abu Amr, Hamza, and Khalaf read the phrase with bi-wariqikum.
rows.anchor: (بورقكم) وهي قراءة أبي عمرو وحمزة وخلف

rows.speaker: أهل مكة
rows.claim: Meccan readers use wariqikum with a still ra and assimilated qaf.
rows.anchor: (ورقكم) - بسكون الراء وإدغام القاف- وهي قراءة أهل مكة

rows.speaker: أكثر القراء
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce the opening waw with fatHa and the ra with kasra in bi-wariqikum.
rows.anchor: وبورقكم بفتح الواو وكسر الراء وهي قراءة أكثر القراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word waraq has variant vocalizations analogous to the cited forms of kabid and kalima.
rows.anchor: ورق) مثل كبد وكبد وكلمة وكلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city they are sent to is Ephesus.
rows.anchor: والمدينة) : أفسوس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr interpret azka food as meat slaughtered lawfully, since most townspeople were Magians and some believers hid their faith.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير: أحل ذبيحة، لأن عامتهم كانوا مجوسا

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses azka as tastier.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك: أطيب

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan glosses azka as better quality.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان: أجود

rows.speaker: يمان بن رئاب
rows.claim: Yaman ibn Ri'ab offers the gloss arfaḍ for azka.
rows.anchor: وقال يمان بن رئاب: أرفض

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses azka as better.
rows.anchor: قتادة: خير

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima glosses azka as more plentiful.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة: أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of zakat means increase and growth; a poem says seven tribes are more azka and better than three.
rows.anchor: وأصل الزكاة الزيادة والنماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq here means sustenance and food; talaṭṭuf means being discreet and gentle while shopping, traveling, and entering the city.
rows.anchor: فليأتكم برزق منه أي قوت وطعام، وليتلطف: وليترفق في الشراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning not to let anyone know means that if Tamlikha is discovered, he should not expose his companions to the same danger.
rows.anchor: أي ولا يعلمن، أي إن ظهر عليه فلا يوقعن إخوانه فيما يقع فيه

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says rajman means insulting and verbally hurting them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: يشتموكم ويؤذوكم بالقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss of rajman is killing; stoning was considered among the worst forms of execution.
rows.anchor: ويقال: يقتلوكم. ويقال: كان من عادتهم القتل بالرجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further gloss takes rajman as reproach or rebuke.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو التوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the townspeople force the youths back into their religion of disbelief, they will never prosper.
rows.anchor: أو يعيدوكم في ملتهم: دينهم الكفر ولن تفلحوا إذا أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Atharna means that God made the townspeople discover or learn about the youths; the verb can mean to discover something or make another discover it.
rows.anchor: عثرت على الشيء إذا اطلعت عليهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the townspeople disputed whether to build a structure or a mosque over the youths; Muslims wanted a mosque because the youths shared their faith.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: تنازعوا في البنيان والمسجد، قال المسلمون: نبني عليهم مسجدا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the dispute concerned bodily resurrection: Muslims affirmed resurrection of body and soul, while others claimed only souls return; the youths' revival demonstrated the former.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: تنازعوا في الأرواح والأجساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reported disputes concerned how long the youths stayed or how many they were.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تنازعوا في قدر لبثهم ومكثهم. وقيل: تنازعوا في عددهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who prevailed and proposed a mosque are identified either as Theodosius and his companions or, in another view, the believers; the latter returns to the first account.
rows.anchor: قال الذين غلبوا على أمرهم يعني تيدوسيس الملك وأصحابه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that when resolved to do something or swear about tomorrow, one should add 'if God wills'; if forgotten, say it when remembered even after a year.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني إذا عزمت على أن تفعل شيئا غدا، أو تحلف على شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction corrects the Prophet's promise to answer questions about the cave youths, the Spirit, and Dhul-Qarnayn without making an exception.
rows.anchor: حين سئل عن المسائل الثلاثة: أصحاب الكهف، والروح، وذي القرنين

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says a servant's faith is incomplete until he qualifies all his speech with an exception.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا يتم إيمان العبد حتى يستثني

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وأبو العالية والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Abu al-Aliya, and al-Hasan interpret remembering God after forgetting as making the exception when one remembers it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وأبو العالية والحسن: معناه: إذا نسيت الاستثناء ثم ذكرت، فاستثن

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima interprets remembering God when one has forgotten as remembering Him when angry.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: معناه: واذكر ربك إذا غضبت

rows.speaker: وهيب
rows.claim: A saying attributed to the Gospel promises that God will remember and spare the person who remembers Him in anger, and urges the wronged not to retaliate.
rows.anchor: مكتوب في الإنجيل: ابن آدم، اذكرني حين تغضب أذكرك حين أغضب

rows.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi interpret the command as referring to prayer, supported by the instruction to pray a forgotten or missed prayer upon remembering.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك والسدي: هذا في الصلاة

rows.speaker: أهل الإشارة
rows.claim: The people of spiritual allusion say to remember God after forgetting everything else; Dhun-Nun says true remembrance makes one forget all things, which God then preserves and replaces.
rows.anchor: معناه واذكر ربك إذا نسيت غيره لأن ذكر الله تعالى إنما يتحقق بعد نسيان غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes forgetting as abandoning remembrance, so the verse commands remembering God after leaving His mention.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه: واذكر ربك إذا تركت ذكره، والنسيان هو الترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks God to keep the Prophet steady on a path nearer to right guidance.
rows.anchor: أي يثبتني على طريق هو أقرب إليه، فأرشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading asks God to guide and support him toward something nearer to what he promised and said would happen, if God wills.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معنا لعل الله أن يهديني ويسددني لأقرب مما وعدتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation asks God either to recall what was forgotten or to guide the speaker to something better than recalling it.
rows.anchor: أو يهديه لما هو خير له من تذكر ما نسيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the questioners asked about the cave story defiantly, God promised evidence and reports of messengers clearer and closer to guidance than that story.
rows.anchor: على وجه العناد أمره الله تعالى أن يخبرهم أن الله سيؤتيه من الحجج والبيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says this phrase is an expiation for forgetting to say 'if God wills' when one remembers the exception.
rows.anchor: فإذا نسي الإنسان فيؤتيه من ذلك. وكفارته أن يقول

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the 300 years and nine years are a report of what the People of the Book said, not God's own report of the cave duration, since the following verse says God knows best.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم: هذا خبر عن أهل الكتاب أنهم قالوا ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: The reading attributed to Ibn Masud adds 'they said' before the statement that the youths stayed in the cave.
rows.anchor: يدل عليه قراءة ابن مسعود: (وقالوا لبثوا في كهفهم)

rows.speaker: مطر الوراق
rows.claim: Matar al-Warraq says the Jews made the duration claim and God rejected it with 'God knows best how long they stayed.'
rows.anchor: وقال مطر الوراق في هذه الآية: هذا شيء قالته اليهود، فرده الله عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says God reports their cave duration, while 'God knows best' refers to time from their souls being taken until the present, known only to God or those He informed.
rows.anchor: وقال الآخرون: هذا إخبار الله عن قدر لبثهم في الكهف

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Christians from Najran knew the 300 years but not the additional nine, so the verse 'God knows best' was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: قالت نصارى نجران: أما الثلاثمائة فقد عرفناها

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read 'three hundred years' with sineen in the genitive and without nunation; the other readers use nunation.
rows.anchor: قرأها حمزة، والكسائي والباقون بالتنوين يعني: ولبثوا في كهفهم سنين ثلاثمائة

rows.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and Muqatil say the first revelation said '300'; after people asked whether these were days or years, 'years' was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك ومقاتل: نزلت: ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة فقالوا: أياما أو سنين؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expressions about seeing and hearing mean that God sees every existing thing and hears every audible thing.
rows.anchor: يعني: ما أبصر الله بكل موجود! وأسمعه بكل مسموع!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one besides God is a guardian or helper for the inhabitants of heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: ما لهم، أي لأهل السماوات والأرض من دونه من دون الله من ولي: ناصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to recite the Qur'an and follow its contents; the author glosses the unchangeable words as God's Book.
rows.anchor: واتل أي واقرأ يا محمد ما أوحي إليك من كتاب ربك، يعني: القرآن

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says no one can alter the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: لا مغير للقرآن

rows.speaker: محمد بن جرير
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Jarir says the unchangeable words are God's threats against those who disobey Him and His Book.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن جرير: يعني: لا مغير لما أوعد بكلماته أهل معاصيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses multahadan as a refuge or protection.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: حرزا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan glosses multahadan as an entrance.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: مدخلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other glosses for multahadan are a way to turn aside or a place of return.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معدلا. وقيل: موئلا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses multahadan as a place of refuge; its root relates to inclining, as with the side niche of a grave.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد ملجأ، وأصله من الميل، ومنه لحد القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed when Uyayna ibn Hisn asked Muhammad to remove poor companions such as Bilal, Suhayb, Khabbab, Ammar, Amir ibn Fuhayra, Mihja, and Salman so nobles could follow him.
rows.anchor: نزلت في عيينة بن حصين الفزاري، وذلك أنه أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to be patient means keep company with those who worship and revere God at dawn and evening, seeking Him rather than worldly gain or display.
rows.anchor: واصبر: واحبس نفسك مع الذين يدعون: يعبدون ربهم ويوقرون ربهم بالغداة والعشي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets dawn and evening as the Fajr and Asr prayers.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: يعني: صلاة الصبح والعصر

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar swears they are the people who perform the obligatory prayers.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار: والذي نفسي بيده إنهم لأهل الصلوات المكتوبة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the verse concerns the seven hundred poor men of the Suffa who stayed at the Prophet's mosque, praying and waiting for the next prayer.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: نزلت هذه الآية في أصحاب الصفة، وكانوا سبعمائة رجل فقراء

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: After the verse came down, the Prophet thanked God for giving him people with whom he was commanded to be patient.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: فلما نزلت هذه الآية قال نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to turn one's eyes away means not to look toward leaders, wealthy people, or nobles seeking worldly adornment.
rows.anchor: ولا تعد عيناك: لا تصرف ولا تجاوز عيناك عنهم إلى غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation places this gaze during the poor worshippers' seeking forgiveness and says the verse rebukes the Prophet for wanting worldly status.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية: ولا تعد عيناك عنهم- مريدا زينة الدنيا- حال خوضهم في الاستغفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making a heart heedless means God left it and caused it to forget His remembrance.
rows.anchor: أي تركنا قلبه وأنسيناه ذكرنا

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya identifies the person whose heart is heedless as Umayya ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi.
rows.anchor: قال أبو العالية: يعني: أمية بن خلف الجمحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another identification names Uyayna ibn Hisn.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: يعني عيينة بن حصين

rows.speaker: قتادة والضحاك ومجاهد
rows.claim: Qatada, al-Dahhak, and Mujahid gloss faratan as waste or loss.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة والضحاك ومجاهد: ضياعا

rows.speaker: داود
rows.claim: Dawud glosses faratan as regret.
rows.anchor: وقال داود: ندما

rows.speaker: حباب
rows.claim: Habab glosses faratan as destruction.
rows.anchor: وقال حباب: هلاكا

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses faratan as opposing the truth.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: مخالفا للحق

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan glosses faratan as excess.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان: سرفا

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses faratan as exceeding the limit.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: مجاوزا للحد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra glosses faratan as abandoned or left behind.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: متروكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss is falsehood; Abu Zayd al-Balkhi takes it as having advanced into evil.
rows.anchor: وقيل: باطلا. وقال أبو زيد البلخي: قدما في الشر

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd relates faratan to a horse that outruns the other horses and speech that gets ahead of its speaker.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: هو من قول العرب: فرس فرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase also means that the person wasted his affairs and days; a believer uses time instead of being used by it.
rows.anchor: قالوا: ان المؤمن من يستعمل الأوقات، ولا تستعمله الأوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-haqq may be nominative as a quoted declaration, as predicate of an omitted subject meaning 'it is the truth,' or as a subject whose predicate is 'from your Lord.'
rows.anchor: الحق: رفع على الحكاية، وقيل: هو رفع على خبر ابتداء مضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth includes the Qur'an, faith, and Muhammad's message; guidance and misguidance are God's decision, and the Prophet is not to expel believers for elite company.
rows.anchor: يعني: ما ذكر من القرآن والإيمان وشأن محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invitation to believe or disbelieve is a warning and threat, not permission to choose freely, like the command to do as one wishes.
rows.anchor: ليس بترخيص وتخيير، إنما هو وعيد وتهديد، كقوله: اعملوا ما شئتم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says whoever God wills to believe believes, and whoever He wills to disbelieve disbelieves, citing that human willing depends on God's will.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: من شاء الله له الايمان آمن، ومن شاء له الكفر كفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A'tadna means prepared or made ready from atad, meaning equipment; the fire is for the wrongdoers, meaning disbelievers.
rows.anchor: إنا أعتدنا: أعددنا وهيأنا، من العتاد، وهو العدة للظالمين: للكافرين نارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse proves that Hell is already created: if it were not existing and prepared, the report would be false, which is impossible of God.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن النار مخلوقة لأنها لو لم تكن مخلوقة موجودة معدة لكان المخبر كذابا

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri reports that the Fire's enclosure consists of four thick walls, each forty years' journey across.
rows.anchor: قال: «سرادق النار أربعة جدر كثف، كل واحد مسيرة أربعين سنة»

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the enclosure is a wall of fire.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هو حائط من نار

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi calls it a neck emerging from the Fire that surrounds disbelievers like an enclosure.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: هو عنق يخرج من النار فيحيط بالكفار كالحظيرة

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybi defines saradiq as the chamber erected around a tent.
rows.anchor: وقال القتيبي: السرادق الحجرة التي تكون حول الفسطاط

rows.speaker: رؤبة
rows.claim: Ruba's line describes the canopy of glory as spread over a person, supporting the word saradiq.
rows.anchor: قال رؤبة: يا حكم بن المنذر بن الجارود

rows.speaker: سلامة بن جندل
rows.claim: Salama ibn Jandal's line uses musardaq for an enclosed roof or building.
rows.anchor: وقال سلامة بن جندل: هو المدخل النعمان بيتا سماؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the enclosure is smoke surrounding disbelievers at resurrection, as in the passage about a shade with three branches in al-Mursalat.
rows.anchor: وهو هاهنا دخان يحيط بالكفار يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Abu Muslim transmits from Abu Sa'id that the water like molten dregs is like oil sediment, and its heat makes facial skin fall when brought near.
rows.anchor: روى أبو مسلم عن أبي سعيد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: بماء كالمهل قال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes al-muhl as thick water like the sediment of oil.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ماء غليظ مثل دردي الزيت

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-A'mash glosses al-muhl as the squeezed residue of oil.
rows.anchor: وقال الأعمش: هو عصارة الزيت

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses al-muhl as pus and blood.
rows.anchor: ومجاهد: القيح والدم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says al-muhl is black water, since Hell, its water and trees, and its inhabitants are black.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك: المهل ماء أسود، وإن جهنم سوداء، ماؤها أسود

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda defines al-muhl as anything melted from the earth's minerals.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: كل ما أذيب من جواهر الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Qatada recounts that Ibn Masud demonstrated al-muhl by melting a gold-and-silver cup in a trench fire until it foamed and liquefied.
rows.anchor: قال: ذكر لنا أن ابن مسعود أهديت له سقاية من ذهب وفضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealthy garden owner, identified as Fatrus, shows his Muslim companion the garden and assumes it will never perish; he doubts the Hour and expects a better return if raised.
rows.anchor: ودخل جنته، يعني: فطروس، أخذ بيد أخيه المسلم يطوف به ويريه إياها

rows.speaker: أهل الحجاز والشام
rows.claim: Readers in the Hijaz and Syria read 'better than the two gardens' in the dual; their codices likewise have the dual form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الحجاز والشام (منهما) على لفظ التثنية، يعني الجنتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munqalaban means a dwelling and return; the garden owner assumes his worldly garden implies something better in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: منقلبا، أي منزلا ومرجعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion's question about creation recalls that God created the man's father and origin from dust, then the man from a drop and fashioned him upright as a male human.
rows.anchor: خلق أباك وأصلك من تراب ثم خلقك من نطفة

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i parses lakinna as a word-order inversion meaning 'but God is my Lord.'
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي: فيه تقديم وتأخير مجازه: لكن الله هو ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another grammatical analysis derives lakinna from lakin ana, with the hamza dropped, the two nuns assimilated, and the alif of ana omitted in connected speech.
rows.anchor: وقال الآخرون: أصله (لكن أنا) فحذفت الهمزة طلبا للخفة

rows.speaker: ابن عامر ويعقوب
rows.claim: Ibn Amir and Yaqub read lakinna with the alif retained in connection, supported by a line of poetry; all readers retain it when pausing.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ويعقوب: (لكنا) ، بإتيان الألف بالوصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion confesses that he does not associate anyone with his Lord.
rows.anchor: ولا أشرك بربي أحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ma sha'a Allah, ma may be nominative as 'it is what God wills' or accusative as the object of 'willed'; an omitted consequence can mean what God wills occurs and what He does not will cannot.
rows.anchor: (ما) في موضع رفع، يعني: هي ما شاء الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that whoever admires something and says 'What God wills; there is no power except through God' will not be harmed by it.
rows.anchor: قال: «من رأى شيئا فأعجبه فقال: ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله
